messages:
maya: Quick sync — thinking of a 'metering' layout that collapses invoices into a compact rail and surfaces token breakdowns inline per project. Uploaded mock: https://img.redwood/mock123.png :point_up: sanjay: Side rail could be good for narrow screens. Concern: it hides monthly totals. What happens on mobile? :thinking: maya: Mobile collapses to a single top toggle, rail only on >=1024px. Mock shows expanded row for invoice items. li: +1 for keeping monthly total prominent. Suggest moving the cumulative spend card to top-left and making the rail dockable. julie: Accessibility notes: need aria-expanded on the rail toggle and a visible focus outline for dock button. Also contrast on the tiny token labels — current color ratio ~2.9:1. sanjay: For chart types, prefer stacked area for cumulative and bar for per-project roughness. Stacked area easy to misread for small projects. maya: Good call. Also proposing a condensed 'token breakdown' row that shows counts and a small sparkline per project. Example snippet: ```
12.4K
``` julie: That code needs aria-hidden on decorative svgs and aria-live region for when numbers update in realtime. Also ensure the count text remains readable at 14px. li: UX question: should invoices be per-org only, or support project-level invoice extraction? Sales asked for project-level CSV export. maya: Plan: invoices default org, but add project filter + export button. UX: filter in rail, export CTA in header. sanjay: Implementation note: lots of DB joins for project invoice export. Need estimate before we promise to Sales. maya: I'll sync with sales and provide an ETA. Quick decision poll — rail vs top tabs for desktop? React with :one: for rail, :two: for tabs. julie: :one: (rail) — better keyboard nav if implemented right. li: :one:. sanjay: :two: (slightly prefer tabs for discoverability) maya: Thanks — leaning rail. I'll update mocks and post revised assets by EOD. :rocket:
